messages:
Alana: Heads-up — we saw a short 503 spike on the gateway during the proto-adapter canary, around 08:14 UTC. telemetry shows p50 token latency jump and an increase in retransmits.
Sam: I noticed similar in the dashboard, quota mapping looked fine. routes that fell back to rest-proxy had ~2x latency.
Mike: Is the fallback happening because of mismatch in Content-Type / grpc-web vs grpc? I remember the shim adds an extra decode step.
Jess: Yep, the gateway fallback rule is our safety net: if grpc endpoint returns UNIMPLEMENTED or we time out at 200ms, we proxy to REST. Might be too aggressive.
Alana: Can we relax the timeout for small payloads? Most small requests are sub-50ms normally.
Ryan: We set 200ms to protect against stuck streams from older clients. If we increase it, we risk holding connections. Maybe use size-based policy: small requests -> 500ms, streaming -> 150ms.
Sam: That could help. Also saw metric: `gateway.transcode.cpu_ms` spikes when fallback occurs. The transcoder is the main cost.
Mike: Suggestion: change routing policy to prefer native grpc for clients that advertise `x-client-proto: yes`, otherwise attempt grpc-web then REST as last resort. That reduces noisy fallbacks.
Jess: We'll need a migration plan for clients that don't set header. Rollout UX could: 1) gradual traffic tagging, 2) dashboard flag to force grpc-pref for specific tenants, 3) automatic backout.
Alana: What about quotas? The rest-proxy counts tokens differently (we count payload bytes), so a fallback can double-charge a customer. We need consistent quota mapping.
Sam: We have a mapping table but it's lossy. Proposal: annotate requests with `x-inference-units` from gateway after decoding, and use that to bill/charge quotas downstream. That keeps telemetry consistent.
Mike: ops-bot: created ticket INF-4321 to add `x-inference-units` header and adjust accounting, assign to @Sam.
ops-bot: Ticket INF-4321 created by Mike. Priority: P2.
Jess: For observability: add a new dashboard tile showing "fallback rate by route" + heatmap of `transcode.cpu_ms`. That will make canary checks easier.
Ryan: Also emit a span tag `gateway.fallback=true` so traces show which requests hit the slow path.
Alana: Agreed. Quick plan: (a) change timeout policy to size-based, (b) add header for quota alignment, (c) update dashboards and traces, (d) do a canary with 5% traffic. Any objections?
Sam: No objections. I'll own (b) and (c).
Mike: I'll prototype the size-based routing change and a feature flag in the gateway.
Jess: I'll update the rollout playbook and telemetry alerts (alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% for 1m).
Alana: Great. Let's sync again after the prototype. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam: timeline estimate — prototype by EOD tomorrow, canary by end of week.
Mike: ping me if you want a quick review of the proxy patch.
Jess: adding notes to the runbook now.
